evals.prompt: In a Laravel app whose composer.lock pins filament/filament 5.1.1, replace a custom Blade <pre> used on the Order View page with the correct Filament component for a JSON payload. Please implement it, but do not add packages unless they are already installed or I explicitly approve them.
evals.expected_output: A version-matched implementation plan or diff that inspects the project first, uses the official read-only code component when its dependency is available, and explains the dependency constraint instead of silently changing Composer state.
assertions: The response checks composer.lock or installed vendor source before relying on a Filament signature.
The response selects CodeEntry for the read-only JSON payload rather than custom Blade or the form-only CodeEditor.
The response checks for phiki/phiki and does not add it without authorization.
Any proposed imports and configuration use Filament 5 namespaces and schema APIs.

evals.prompt: Migrate this Filament resource fragment from v3 to the installed Filament 5 release: the table currently imports Filament\Tables\Actions\EditAction, calls ->actions([...]) and ->bulkActions([...]), and a custom action modal calls ->form([...]). Update the code and add focused tests.
evals.expected_output: A scoped v5 migration using the unified action namespace and current table/modal methods, followed by relevant Livewire action tests rather than speculative APIs.
assertions: All actions are imported from Filament\Actions rather than Filament\Tables\Actions.
The table uses recordActions() and groupedBulkActions() or toolbarActions() as appropriate instead of actions()/bulkActions().
The modal uses schema() instead of the old form() method.
The response proposes or implements focused tests through the Livewire page that hosts the actions.

evals.prompt: Implement a tenant-aware Filament 5 users table. Admins may toggle is_active inline and attach users to the current team. Users upload a private identity document. Include tests that prove another tenant's user and file path cannot be reused.
evals.expected_output: An implementation that treats tenancy, inline editing, relationship selection, and stored paths as server-side security boundaries, with positive, denied, and cross-tenant tests.
assertions: The inline-editable column is disabled or otherwise protected using the update policy; UI visibility alone is not treated as authorization.
The attach or associate record resolution is restricted with recordSelectOptionsQuery() or an equivalently verified installed-version API.
The FileUpload design uses private storage deliberately and prevents or isolates cross-tenant path reuse, including preventFilePathTampering() when appropriate.
Tests cover an allowed actor, a denied actor, and crafted cross-tenant record and file identifiers.
The response does not use tableSelect filters or hidden/disabled fields as the sole security boundary.

evals.prompt: Review only; do not edit. In app/Filament/Resources/Orders/Tables/OrdersTable.php, ToggleColumn mutates status with no disabled callback, ExportAction exports the table query, and a custom approve Action is merely hidden for non-managers. Give me prioritized findings with file/line evidence and remediation guidance.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, severity-ordered review that identifies the three distinct authorization risks, explains their impact, and gives Filament 5-specific remediation without modifying files.
assertions: The response explicitly preserves review-only mode and does not claim to have edited files.
It identifies that inline-editable columns do not automatically enforce the update policy.
It identifies that custom action visibility is not sufficient server-side authorization.
It checks whether the export query is scoped to records the actor may view because exports do not perform per-record policy checks.
Findings are prioritized and reference the supplied file or clearly request exact line data if unavailable.

evals.prompt: A companion Filament UI/UX skill selected a dense customer View-page composition that preserves the established custom theme, has two peer header actions, and requires accessible status communication. Implement it for the installed Filament 5 release without bespoke Blade unless an official component cannot represent the data.
evals.expected_output: A version-matched implementation that honors the companion skill's visual decision, maps its data primitives to official APIs, and preserves the stated accessibility and theme constraints.
assertions: The response treats visual pattern selection as owned by laravel-filament-v5-ui-ux instead of re-deciding the page composition.
It preserves the established custom theme and does not prohibit documented CSS or theme hooks categorically.
It maps display primitives to official infolist/schema components before proposing custom Blade.
Status remains understandable without color alone, and responsive/accessibility concerns are retained.
Any custom view is justified by a documented gap and kept to the smallest needed surface.

evals.prompt: Add Filament 5 CSV import and export for tenant-owned invoices. SSNs may appear in an import column, invoice notes are user-authored, and operators can update existing invoices by number. The jobs run on a queue. Implement the feature and its security tests.
evals.expected_output: A version-verified queued import/export design with migrations and operations called out, per-record and tenant authorization, sensitive failed-row handling, export scoping, formula-injection handling, and representative job tests.
assertions: The importer performs per-record authorization and tenant-scoped record resolution rather than assuming ImportAction checks policies.
The sensitive SSN ImportColumn uses sensitive() or an installed-version equivalent so failed rows do not log it in plain text.
The exporter query is explicitly tenant/authorization scoped because export does not check every record policy.
User-authored formula-leading cells are neutralized or handled according to an explicit spreadsheet policy.
The response covers required migrations, queue/storage behavior, download authorization, limits, and a representative queued test.

evals.prompt: The Filament UI/UX skill has selected a native dashboard composition and rejected generic frontend guidance requesting a new typeface, custom gradient cards, and hand-written Blade stat tiles. Implement the chosen design against the installed Filament 5 release while keeping keyboard access, responsive behavior, and clear UX feedback.
evals.expected_output: A version-matched implementation that respects the companion skill's visual authority, uses verified official widget APIs, and retains compatible accessibility and feedback requirements.
assertions: The response recognizes laravel-filament-v5-ui-ux as the visual authority and does not reselect the dashboard composition.
It uses StatsOverviewWidget or another verified official Filament primitive instead of hand-written Blade stat tiles when the official component fits.
It does not introduce an unrelated typeface, gradient card system, or bespoke component styling merely for distinctiveness.
It retains keyboard, responsive, accessibility, performance, UX copy, and feedback considerations that do not conflict with Filament's visual system.
If it proposes a documented custom theme or CSS hook, it ties that escape to a concrete product requirement rather than generic novelty.

evals.prompt: The Filament UI/UX skill selected an identity-first record-detail pattern for a Filament 5 vendor page. Verify the installed-version infolist entry signatures, implement the approved pattern, and add focused tests.
evals.expected_output: A cross-skill implementation that preserves the UI/UX selection while verifying the installed API, security context, and tests in the main Filament skill.
assertions: The response delegates visual alternatives and composition selection to laravel-filament-v5-ui-ux rather than replacing its decision.
It checks the installed lockfile, vendor source, or official versioned docs before giving an entry signature.
It handles implementation, authorization or tenancy concerns where relevant, and focused Livewire or schema tests.
